title: Módulos, packaging y CLI profesional
review_contracts: PYARCANA — MODO REVISOR ESCÉPTICO Y ANTI-COMPLACENCIA
Solarized Website Content Comprehension Auditor & Rewriter

learner_entry_state.credit_rule: Only concepts marked USABLE in the effective prior ledger count as learned.

roadmap_expectation.T1: modules, imports, namespaces, __main__, circular dependencies and public API
roadmap_expectation.T2: src layout, pyproject.toml, builds, versioning and compatibility
roadmap_expectation.T3: argparse, subcommands, exit codes, stdin/stdout/stderr and help
roadmap_expectation.T4: file/env/flag precedence, secrets, defaults and early configuration validation
roadmap_expectation.gate: installable CLI ingest|normalize|compare|report with clean help, unambiguous errors and business logic separated from I/O

live_site.note: Public fetch returned DisabledError; no hydrated-render parity claim is made.

used_for: environment keys and values are strings

confirmed_findings.evidence: CP-N1-B/C and gate remain internal curriculum labels without a stable learner-facing expansion.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Due to this problem, a reasonable learner can be unsure whether CP-N1-B/C denotes a package, project increment, assessment gate or file.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Expand each identifier once in learner language before reusing the abbreviation.

confirmed_findings.evidence: jobRelevance says command-line option overrides file and file overrides environment, while the outcome and T4-A define flags > env > file > defaults.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Due to this problem, a reasonable learner can implement two different precedence orders depending on which paragraph they copy.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Use one canonical order everywhere; retain flags > env > file > defaults because T4 and the outcome already teach it.

confirmed_findings.evidence: The example claims the import path is usable without CLI side effects, but executes print('import_safe', ...) at top level, so importing the module prints output.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Due to this problem, a reasonable learner can believe an import-safe module may execute arbitrary prints as long as the CLI function itself is guarded.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Move every demonstrative print under main()/the __main__ guard; leave only definitions at import time unless initialization is explicitly intended.

confirmed_findings.evidence: T1-A says python -m familiarity_core runs the package without fighting sys.path; T2-A correctly says src layout prevents importing the package from the repository until it is installed. PyPA states src layout requires project installation.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Due to this problem, a reasonable learner can run python -m familiarity_core from an uninstalled src-layout checkout and conclude the package or __main__.py is broken when the real problem is discoverability.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: State that python -m familiarity_core works after the package is discoverable, normally after python -m pip install -e . in this course.

confirmed_findings.evidence: __all__ is presented as the public API list the team can import with confidence. Python primarily uses __all__ to control from package import *; it does not prevent explicit imports of omitted/private names.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Due to this problem, a reasonable learner can believe __all__ enforces privacy or stability at runtime.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Say __all__ documents/controls wildcard export; public API stability remains a project contract backed by documentation, reexports and naming conventions.

confirmed_findings.evidence: Circular imports are reduced to 'Python se enreda' and a shared util is prescribed as first resource. The actual failure mode is access to partially initialized modules/names; some cycles execute and some fail depending on when names are needed.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Due to this problem, a reasonable learner can cargo-cult lazy imports or utility modules without diagnosing the dependency direction that caused the cycle.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Add one sentence explaining partially initialized modules and prefer refactoring dependency direction before lazy-import workarounds.

confirmed_findings.evidence: S10-package-layout is attached to Dependencias cíclicas y API pública, while S10-config-precedence is attached to Layout src, pyproject.toml y builds, before configuration precedence is taught in T4-A.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Due to this problem, a reasonable learner can encounter visual explanations before the concept they are meant to explain and associate the wrong diagram with the wrong subtopic.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Move package-layout to T2-A and config-precedence to T4-A without rewriting either figure.

confirmed_findings.evidence: The package declares requires-python = >=3.11 although S01 explicitly requires Python 3.12+ and says the course uses Python 3.12.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Due to this problem, a reasonable learner can publish metadata claiming support for Python 3.11 even though the course never validated the package against that runtime.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Use requires-python = >=3.12 unless the project actually tests and supports 3.11.

confirmed_findings.evidence: The opening correctly says [project.scripts] is what creates the installed command, but the canonical pyproject fragment omits [project.scripts]. Installing that demonstrated metadata cannot create the promised familiarity command.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Due to this problem, a reasonable learner can perform an editable install, find no familiarity executable, and have no lesson-local artifact showing what entry point is missing.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix:
Add [project.scripts]
familiarity = 'familiarity_core.cli:main' and show __main__.py delegating to the same main function.

confirmed_findings.evidence: Editable install is described as reflecting changes without reinstalling, without limiting that claim to source-code changes. PyPA explicitly describes editable reflection for source code; metadata, dependency and script changes can require reinstall/rebuild.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Due to this problem, a reasonable learner can edit pyproject entry points or dependencies and expect the installed metadata/wrapper to update automatically.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Say Python source edits are reflected; reinstall after changing packaging metadata, dependencies or console-script declarations.

confirmed_findings.evidence: The section says the program uses only the standard library while its build-system requires setuptools>=61, a third-party build dependency. Runtime dependencies and build dependencies are not distinguished.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Due to this problem, a reasonable learner can conclude the project has zero third-party dependencies of any kind and misunderstand why the build environment downloads setuptools.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Distinguish runtime dependencies from build-system dependencies; runtime may be stdlib-only while packaging still uses a build backend.

confirmed_findings.evidence: The lesson teaches breaking -> MAJOR as a general rule while using version 0.1.0 and only briefly saying 0.x is more flexible. SemVer 2.0 states 0.y.z is initial development and the public API should not be considered stable.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Due to this problem, a reasonable learner can treat 0.1.0 as a stable SemVer contract or jump to 1.0.0 merely because any pre-1.0 API changed.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Separate the course's pre-1.0 policy from SemVer 1.x rules; define exactly how 0.y.z changes are versioned before declaring 1.0.0.

confirmed_findings.evidence: try_parse([]) catches argparse's SystemExit(2), returns integer 2 and the surrounding demonstration keeps running. The example prints code 2 but does not make the Python process exit 2; it also never demonstrates runtime/business code 1.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Due to this problem, a reasonable learner can repeat the S08/S09 misconception that printing/returning an integer inside a helper proves the operating-system process status.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Demonstrate the actual entrypoint boundary with raise SystemExit(main(...)) or sys.exit(main()), and separately show a real runtime-error path mapping to 1.

confirmed_findings.evidence: The prose says main(argv) -> int lets tests simulate invalid usage and receive code 2, but default ArgumentParser.parse_args raises SystemExit(2) on usage errors. The code avoids this only by inventing a separate try_parse wrapper, not the promised main architecture.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Due to this problem, a reasonable learner can write a main function expected to return 2, then see a test abort with SystemExit instead.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Teach that argparse owns usage errors and raises SystemExit(2) by default; tests assert that behavior, while main returns 0/1 for normal/runtime paths, or deliberately customize parser error handling and explain the tradeoff.

confirmed_findings.evidence: The paragraph promises data on stdout and diagnostics on stderr, but the canonical demo uses print for the data, the literal label '--- stderr ---', and the log contents. Capturing the example shows stderr is empty and every line goes to stdout.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Due to this problem, a reasonable learner can copy the example into a JSON-producing CLI and contaminate stdout with diagnostic text while believing it is on stderr.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Use print(data, file=sys.stdout) for data and print/logging StreamHandler(sys.stderr) for diagnostics; demonstrate captured stdout and stderr separately.
confirmed_findings.execution_evidence: Exact demo produced all lines on stdout and zero lesson-generated stderr.

confirmed_findings.evidence: The theory promises support for path or '-' as stdin and discusses pipes twice, but the code never reads sys.stdin, never branches on '-', and never opens an input path.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Due to this problem, a reasonable learner cannot implement the promised pipe contract from the lesson before practice.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Add a minimal read_input(path) example: if path == '-', read sys.stdin; otherwise read the named Path.

confirmed_findings.evidence: The only shell example uses cat data.json, while S01 explicitly supports Windows/PowerShell as a first-class path.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Due to this problem, a Windows learner can think stdin piping is unavailable or that their shell is wrong when cat is not the documented command for their environment.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Label Unix/macOS and PowerShell examples separately, or use a platform-neutral conceptual pipe plus both concrete commands.

confirmed_findings.evidence: The lesson's core outcome is flags > env > file > defaults, but the example receives four already-constructed dictionaries. It never reads an OS environment variable, never reads a config file, and never connects argparse Namespace values to flags. T4-B then calls .env 'the environment-variable file' even though Python stdlib does not automatically load .env files.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Due to this problem, a reasonable learner can understand dictionary merge order yet still be unable to implement any of the three real configuration sources, or assume creating .env automatically populates os.environ.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Show one concrete source per layer: argparse flags, os.environ, a documented config file format, and defaults; state that .env is only a file convention and requires explicit loading/parsing.

confirmed_findings.evidence: Prose says None in flags means 'not passed', but code filters None from file_cfg and env_cfg too. That silently treats explicit None in every layer as missing.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Due to this problem, a reasonable learner can lose an explicit clear/disable value from a configuration source and believe it was absent.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Apply the 'None means not passed' rule only to the layer whose parser uses that sentinel, or represent absence with omitted keys/a dedicated sentinel.

confirmed_findings.evidence: The text says invalid startup config must fail-fast, but the demo catches RuntimeError, prints the message and completes normally. This repeats the exact S08/S09 process-status defect at the point S10 was supposed to repair it.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Due to this problem, a reasonable learner can ship a CLI that logs a configuration failure but exits 0, causing schedulers and CI to mark the run successful.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: At the application boundary print a sanitized diagnostic to stderr and return/exit 1; do not swallow the fatal exception in the canonical fail-fast demonstration.

confirmed_findings.evidence: env_cfg is shown as an ordinary typed dict even though Python os.environ keys and values are strings. Numeric/boolean settings require explicit parsing before merge/validation.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Due to this problem, a reasonable learner can let jobs='4' override jobs=1 and later hit type-dependent behavior while believing the precedence merge preserved the configuration type.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: State that environment values arrive as strings and parse each supported key into its contract type before merging.

confirmed_findings.evidence: The section criterion is an installable package with useful CLI, but theory only prints a TOML string and a layout path. It never creates the actual artifact, runs python -m pip install -e ., invokes familiarity --help, or verifies python -m familiarity_core. The I Do explicitly says the real install lives in You Do.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Due to this problem, a reasonable learner reaches practice without having seen the complete packaging mechanism that the lesson's gate requires.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Add one compact reference artifact in theory: real pyproject.toml, src/familiarity_core/cli.py, __main__.py, editable-install command and one successful --help invocation.

rejected_findings.hypothesis: src layout itself is unnecessary ceremony
rejected_findings.reason: PyPA explicitly documents that src layout prevents accidental use of the repository copy and requires installation, which is exactly the behavior S10 needs to teach.

rejected_findings.hypothesis: argparse does not use exit code 2 for invalid usage
rejected_findings.reason: Python argparse documents stderr + status 2 by default. The defect is that S10 catches that SystemExit and presents the returned integer as process evidence.
The idiom is correct. The defect is the top-level print that violates the import-safe claim.

rejected_findings.hypothesis: project.scripts is the wrong mechanism for an installed CLI
rejected_findings.reason: PyPA specifies [project.scripts] as console-script entry points. The defect is its omission from the canonical artifact.

rejected_findings.hypothesis: underscore-prefixed helpers are truly private and inaccessible
rejected_findings.reason: The lesson itself calls underscore a convention. The remaining issue is overloading __all__ as if it were the full public-API enforcement mechanism.

rejected_findings.hypothesis: editable installation never reflects changes without reinstall
rejected_findings.reason: PyPA confirms ordinary Python source edits are reflected. Only the absolute wording needs a metadata/entry-point caveat.

rejected_findings.hypothesis: flags > env > file > defaults is intrinsically wrong
rejected_findings.reason: It is a defensible policy. The confirmed defect is that jobRelevance teaches a different order.
Those rules are correct for stable public APIs. The unresolved teaching defect is applying them too broadly around 0.y.z.

paragraph_reviews.current_excerpt: Alguien del equipo necesita correr tu limpieza... notebook... ruta en línea catorce.
paragraph_reviews.reason: Concrete actor/problem/operational outcome; attack found no material technical defect.
paragraph_reviews.improved_content: Alguien del equipo necesita correr tu limpieza de datos el lunes a las siete. Le pasas la carpeta y empiezas a explicar: abre el notebook, ejecuta las celdas en este orden y cambia una ruta escrita dentro del código. Eso todavía depende de instrucciones orales, no de una interfaz reproducible.

paragraph_reviews.current_excerpt: pyproject.toml... [project.scripts]... pip install -e . convierte...
paragraph_reviews.improved_content: `pyproject.toml` describe cómo se construye e instala el proyecto. Para crear un comando instalable debes declarar además `[project.scripts]`, por ejemplo `familiarity = "familiarity_core.cli:main"`. Después de `python -m pip install -e .`, el instalador crea el wrapper del comando y lo conecta con esa función.

paragraph_reviews.current_excerpt: CLI... programa se ejecuta escribiendo una palabra... notebook no.
paragraph_reviews.reason: Notebook automation is possible; the benefit is a stable shell interface, not impossibility of scheduling notebooks.
paragraph_reviews.improved_content: Una CLI es una interfaz de línea de comandos: ejecutas una orden estable desde la terminal con subcomandos y opciones. Esa interfaz es fácil de documentar, automatizar y encadenar; un notebook también puede automatizarse, pero no ofrece por sí solo el mismo contrato de argumentos, salidas y códigos de proceso.

paragraph_reviews.current_excerpt: precedencia... flag pisa archivo y archivo entorno
paragraph_reviews.improved_content: El mismo valor puede llegar desde defaults, archivo, variables de entorno o flags. Esta sección usa un único orden: **flag > entorno > archivo > default**. La primera capa que exista al leer de mayor a menor prioridad determina el valor efectivo.

paragraph_reviews.current_excerpt: ¿qué necesito saber... --help... usa solo biblioteca estándar
paragraph_reviews.improved_content: La pregunta es qué necesita saber alguien que nunca vio el repositorio para ejecutar el comando correctamente. `--help` debe cubrir el uso inmediato; README documenta instalación y configuración. El código de ejecución puede depender solo de la biblioteca estándar aunque el proceso de build use una herramienta de packaging como setuptools.

paragraph_reviews.current_excerpt: Bloque de referencia...
paragraph_reviews.improved_content: Bloque de referencia. Orden de los subtemas, alcance y criterio de cierre.

paragraph_reviews.current_excerpt: T1 módulos... T2 paquetes... T3 CLI... T4 precedencia
paragraph_reviews.improved_content: T1 trata módulos y entrypoints; T2 construye el paquete; T3 hace observable la CLI y sus streams/códigos; T4 conecta fuentes reales de configuración con una precedencia única.

paragraph_reviews.current_excerpt: S08 + S09... códigos 0,1,2 según fallo
paragraph_reviews.improved_content: Integra el ETL de S08 y el logging de S09, pero S10 debe cerrar por primera vez la frontera del proceso: éxito termina 0, error de ejecución termina 1 y uso inválido de argparse termina 2.

paragraph_reviews.current_excerpt: paquete instalable editable... cuatro subcomandos... ayuda
paragraph_reviews.improved_content: Cierre: `python -m pip install -e .` instala el paquete y crea `familiarity`; `familiarity --help` muestra `ingest`, `normalize`, `compare` y `report`; la lógica de negocio puede importarse sin ejecutar la CLI.

paragraph_reviews.current_excerpt: config/schema no cuadran... se detiene
paragraph_reviews.improved_content: Si la configuración o el schema son inválidos al arrancar, el comando escribe un diagnóstico sanitizado en stderr y termina con estado no-cero antes de procesar datos.

paragraph_reviews.current_excerpt: imports cargan módulo una vez... __name__... python -m... __main__.py
paragraph_reviews.improved_content: En una ejecución normal, el primer import ejecuta el código de inicialización del módulo y Python conserva el módulo en `sys.modules` para reutilizarlo. `__name__` identifica el módulo; vale `__main__` en el entorno de máximo nivel. Con este layout `python -m familiarity_core` funciona cuando el paquete ya es localizable, normalmente después del editable install, y ejecuta `familiarity_core/__main__.py`.

paragraph_reviews.current_excerpt: guard protege CLI; __all__ documenta API pública
paragraph_reviews.improved_content: La guarda `if __name__ == "__main__":` evita ejecutar el entrypoint durante un import. `__all__` controla qué nombres exporta un `from paquete import *`; puede apoyar la documentación de la fachada, pero no impide que alguien importe explícitamente un helper interno.

paragraph_reviews.current_excerpt: imports circulares... tercer módulo... lazy import...
paragraph_reviews.improved_content: Un ciclo A→B→A puede exponer un módulo todavía parcialmente inicializado. Primero revisa si la dependencia común puede moverse a una capa que ambos módulos importen sin volver hacia atrás. Un import local puede diferir el ciclo, pero úsalo solo cuando entiendas por qué esa dependencia debe ser diferida.

paragraph_reviews.current_excerpt: _ marca helpers privados... fachada reexporta estable
paragraph_reviews.improved_content: El prefijo `_` comunica que un nombre es interno; no lo vuelve inaccesible. La fachada reexporta y documenta los nombres que el proyecto promete mantener estables. Los consumidores deben depender de esa interfaz documentada, no de helpers internos.

paragraph_reviews.current_excerpt: API pública pequeña... SemVer añadir minor, eliminar major
paragraph_reviews.improved_content: Mantén una API pública pequeña. Cuando declares 1.0.0 y una API estable, SemVer usa MINOR para funcionalidad compatible y MAJOR para cambios incompatibles. Antes de 1.0 define y documenta explícitamente tu política de cambios.

paragraph_reviews.current_excerpt: lazy import evita ciclos y acelera arranque
paragraph_reviews.improved_content: Un import diferido puede retrasar el costo de cargar una dependencia opcional y, en casos justificados, evitar acceder demasiado pronto a un módulo parcialmente inicializado. No sustituye el análisis de la dirección de dependencias.

paragraph_reviews.current_excerpt: src layout... pyproject... build backend
paragraph_reviews.improved_content: En src layout el paquete importable vive bajo `src/`, por lo que normalmente debes instalar el proyecto antes de importarlo. `pyproject.toml` declara metadata del proyecto y el build backend. El código runtime puede ser stdlib-only aunque el build use setuptools como dependencia de construcción.

paragraph_reviews.current_excerpt: pip install -e . refleja cambios al toque
paragraph_reviews.improved_content: `python -m pip install -e .` instala el proyecto en modo editable. Los cambios en archivos Python se reflejan sin reinstalar; cambios en dependencias, entrypoints u otra metadata de packaging pueden requerir repetir la instalación.

paragraph_reviews.current_excerpt: ModuleNotFoundError... venv, import name, cwd shadows
paragraph_reviews.improved_content: Si el import falla tras instalar, confirma primero que `python -m pip` y `python` son el mismo entorno; después verifica el nombre bajo `src/` y finalmente si otro archivo/directorio del cwd está sombreando el paquete.

paragraph_reviews.current_excerpt: SemVer MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH... 0.x flexible...
paragraph_reviews.improved_content: SemVer 2.0 reserva 0.y.z para desarrollo inicial: la API todavía no se considera estable. Cuando declares 1.0.0, PATCH corrige sin romper contrato, MINOR añade funcionalidad compatible y MAJOR introduce incompatibilidades.

paragraph_reviews.current_excerpt: requires-python y dependencies pinadas con criterio
paragraph_reviews.improved_content: Declara `requires-python = ">=3.12"`, coherente con el runtime del curso. Para dependencias, especifica restricciones justificadas; no llames 'pin' a una versión mínima si no estás fijando una versión exacta.

paragraph_reviews.current_excerpt: CHANGELOG... deprecar un minor antes
paragraph_reviews.improved_content: Mantén un CHANGELOG breve. Tras 1.0, documenta deprecaciones en una versión compatible antes de retirar una API en un release major. Si sigues en 0.y.z, aplica la política pre-1.0 que acabas de declarar.

paragraph_reviews.current_excerpt: argparse + subparsers...
paragraph_reviews.improved_content: `ArgumentParser` define la interfaz de argumentos y los subparsers definen cada subcomando. Cada opción debe indicar qué recibe y para qué sirve en un `help=` que el operador pueda entender sin leer código.

paragraph_reviews.current_excerpt: exit 0/2/1... CI depende
paragraph_reviews.improved_content: Distingue el número que retorna una función del estado del proceso. En esta CLI: 0 = éxito; argparse termina 2 por uso inválido; un fallo de ejecución controlado debe llegar al entrypoint y terminar 1. CI y schedulers observan el estado del proceso, no un número impreso.

paragraph_reviews.current_excerpt: main(argv)->int... sys.exit(main())... unit test invalid usage
paragraph_reviews.improved_content: Haz que `main(argv)` retorne 0/1 para las rutas que controla y que el entrypoint haga `sys.exit(main())`. Con argparse por defecto, errores de uso lanzan `SystemExit(2)` antes de que `main` retorne; los tests deben comprobar esa excepción o ejecutar el CLI como proceso.

paragraph_reviews.current_excerpt: stdout datos; stderr logs; print ok rompe pipe
paragraph_reviews.improved_content: stdout contiene exclusivamente el dato que otro programa consumirá. stderr contiene diagnósticos y progreso. Escribe explícitamente `print(data, file=sys.stdout)` y `print(message, file=sys.stderr)` o configura logging hacia stderr.

paragraph_reviews.current_excerpt: path o - para stdin... cat data.json
paragraph_reviews.improved_content: Convención del curso: si el argumento de entrada es `-`, lee `sys.stdin`; de lo contrario abre el path. En Unix/macOS puedes producir el stream con `cat`; en PowerShell usa `Get-Content -Raw` o el comando equivalente documentado.

paragraph_reviews.current_excerpt: repite soporte -; StringIO; no print progreso
paragraph_reviews.improved_content: En tests puedes reemplazar stdin/stdout/stderr por `StringIO`, pero la demo debe mantenerlos separados. El stream de diagnóstico simula stderr y nunca se vuelve a imprimir sobre stdout dentro del mismo contrato.

paragraph_reviews.current_excerpt: precedencia flags > env > file > defaults
paragraph_reviews.improved_content: Precedencia única: flag > variable de entorno > archivo > default. Muestra de dónde sale cada capa antes de fusionarla: `argparse` produce flags, `os.environ` produce strings del entorno y el lector del archivo produce configuración persistida.

paragraph_reviews.current_excerpt: None flags = no pasado
paragraph_reviews.improved_content: Usa `None` como 'flag no pasado' solo si tu parser reserva ese valor para ausencia. Las variables de entorno llegan como strings y deben convertirse al tipo esperado antes del merge. No confundas una clave ausente con un valor explícito de otra capa.

paragraph_reviews.current_excerpt: merge_config puro; dicts por capa
paragraph_reviews.improved_content: Separa dos pasos: primero adapta cada fuente a un dict tipado y documentado; después aplica un `merge_config` puro en el orden default→archivo→entorno→flag. Así el merge no necesita adivinar si `None` significa ausencia o valor.

paragraph_reviews.current_excerpt: .env archivo de variables de entorno; gitignore
paragraph_reviews.improved_content: Las variables de entorno reales llegan al proceso mediante el sistema operativo y se leen con `os.environ`. Un archivo `.env` es solo una convención de texto; Python no lo carga automáticamente. Si el curso permanece stdlib-only, usa variables de entorno reales o un archivo de configuración que el programa lea explícitamente. Mantén secretos fuera del repositorio.

paragraph_reviews.current_excerpt: validate_config al arranque...
paragraph_reviews.improved_content: Valida la configuración antes de procesar datos. Si falta una clave necesaria, produce un diagnóstico sanitizado que nombre clave y subcomando y devuelve ese fallo al entrypoint para que el proceso termine no-cero.

paragraph_reviews.current_excerpt: fail-fast config... jamás token traceback
paragraph_reviews.improved_content: Fail-fast significa que la ejecución no continúa con datos después de detectar configuración inválida. El handler de frontera escribe el diagnóstico en stderr sin valores secretos y termina el proceso con estado de error; imprimir el mensaje y continuar hasta un exit 0 no es fail-fast.

artifact_reviews.note: Move top-level print under guarded main; keep import path side-effect free.
Use real TOML artifact, Python >=3.12, and [project.scripts].

artifact_reviews.execution_check: try_parse([]) returned integer 2 after catching SystemExit, while the enclosing process path remains successful unless that code is propagated to sys.exit.
Exact lesson demo produced all diagnostic labels/log text on stdout and no lesson-generated stderr.

artifact_reviews.note: Teach acquisition/parsing of layers before pure merge.
Canonical fail-fast path must actually reach process failure.

priority_repairs: Make import-safe example actually side-effect free.
Tie python -m execution to installed/discoverable src-layout package.
Add [project.scripts] and a real package/CLI artifact.
Demonstrate actual OS exit 0/1/2, not printed integers.
Make stdout/stderr physically separate in code.
Show real flag/env/file acquisition and .env limitation.
Preserve missing-vs-null semantics in config layers.
Make config fail-fast actually exit non-zero.

rules: S11 is the first canonical OOP/classes section. Custom exception classes shown in S09 and library classes used in S10 do not count as learned class/inheritance semantics.
Do not assume __main__, public API, console entrypoints or process exit semantics are safe prerequisites; S10 leaves all of them PARTIAL/MISCONCEPTION_RISK.
S11 may treat src layout as USABLE, but packaging metadata and import mechanics need local bridges if architecture examples depend on them.
Configuration/fail-fast remains unsafe; domain-model constructors must not silently inherit the idea that logging an error equals failing the process.
S11 must repair the earlier invariant misconception when teaching class invariants/states.
JSON/provenance remain PARTIAL from S08 and should not become hidden prerequisites for serialization examples.
